instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Hope Keeps Moving
cards.instruction: Turn every disappointment into a new reason the desired outcome is delayed, redirected, or becoming more meaningful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The hall rejected our wedding booking. Remember when I made you revise a plan instead of throwing it away? We're finding somewhere better.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Every venue is booked for June.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then September. You always rushed to hand things in; three more months will do us good.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My parents can't travel in September.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we go to them. Their garden. You can stop treating every correction as a failure; put the people in the plan first this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our bookshop failed here. Don't box everything together; I taught you to look for the reader before choosing the shelf. We've been looking in the wrong place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We have no moving money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One shelf, then. You used to need a whole window before you could choose three books. This is making us precise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can get us a stall by the bus stop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good eye. People with ten minutes and nothing to read. Pack the short stories first; you're finally showing me the customer instead of the shop.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Comfort Everyone Else
cards.instruction: Meet every painful moment by comforting someone else more intensely while your own distress becomes harder to hide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've both been laid off. Sit down; take a tissue. Remember how I got you breathing again after your first angry caller?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're wiping your eyes on your sleeve.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Never mind my sleeve. Breathe out slowly. You always stopped halfway when you were upset. I'll open these for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're shaking too much to get the box open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take the box. Both hands, that's it. I'll make your tea when mine settle. You shouldn't have to look after yourself today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Soup's ready. The choir rejected us, but you still have to eat. How often did I make you bring a sandwich to rehearsals?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've set a bowl for yourself too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To keep you company. You used to leave half yours when nobody watched. Let me butter your bread.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sit with me. I don't want you crying in the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. Take my bread too; I can't swallow yet. Slowly, small bites. You always tried to get this part over with.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Emotional Interest
cards.instruction: Treat comfort, vulnerability, and forgiveness as investments that must eventually be repaid with equal emotional risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I told your mother I'm scared she dislikes me. You used to practise difficult openings with me. I've done this one for real; your turn on Sunday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't ask you to tell her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You never asked for the demonstrations, either, but you learned. I risked looking foolish. Give me an answer that costs you as much.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm scared she'll like you more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. That's the first honest answer you've given me. Now say it to her over lunch. I didn't do my demonstration in private.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll stay while you tell me why you hid the debt. I used to sit through every difficult answer with you. Someday I need you to risk as much with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you keeping score?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not marks. I stayed when you expected me to leave. When I need the truth from you, I want an answer that frightens you this much.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I kept borrowing because I wanted you to be proud of me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's harder than admitting the amount. Good. You can count that as a first payment. I'm still here; tell me the rest.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Ready on My Terms
cards.instruction: Agree to be honest, hopeful, or vulnerable only in forms that preserve your emotional safety.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll talk about the rent argument. One question at a time, the way I taught you. Don't start with the whole year.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole year matters. You've been pulling away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Good, you've named what worries you. Now ask one thing and let me finish the answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Were you going to move out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I packed a bag. It's still upstairs. Don't rush to the next question—you always did that when an answer frightened you. Let this one sit for a minute.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll talk about coming home, but I'll sit by the door. Take the chair where I used to coach your speeches. Tonight let me find the words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you planning to run?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Knowing I can leave helps me stay. Don't jump to the ending; you used to lose half your speech that way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can stop when you need to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I want to come home. Don't hand me a key yet. One sentence at a time, the way we practised.

cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: The Same Ending
cards.instruction: Use every new emotional detail as evidence that the same feared ending is becoming inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Take care.' You finally learned to end a message kindly. That's exactly what he wrote before he left me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said you had a cold. I meant get better.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're remembering all my little rules about consideration. He wanted me well before leaving too; it made him feel less guilty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll bring soup tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you remembered feeding someone helps. You've become very good at this goodbye. Will the soup come in a container you don't need back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You cancelled lunch so politely. I spent years teaching you to say no, and now you're starting the same way my last partner did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've only cancelled lunch. I'm exhausted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, using 'I' instead of blaming me. He was tired too, just before seeing me became another job.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tomorrow, then? I'll book our usual table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A public place. You remembered my advice about difficult conversations. Book the corner, please. I don't want the whole room hearing me ask you to stay.
